newsitem.title: USA: Unocal to buy back stock, cut debt -- CEO.
newsitem.headline: Unocal to buy back stock, cut debt -- CEO.

text.p: Unocal Corp plans to buy back stock and cut debt with proceeds from the sale of its downstream assets to Tosco Corp late last year, Roger Beach, Unocal chief executive officer, said in a statement.
"We expect to initially redeploy the proceeds into reducing our debt and buying back some of our common stock," Beach said.
Unocal's total debt fell to $3.06 billion at the end of 1996, down $648 million from the end of 1995, the company said.
The sale of its downstream and California oil and gas properties will enable the company to look into overseas projects, Beach said.
Overseas growth will focus on Asia, where Unocal's share of Thailand's natural gas production averaged more than 612 million cubic feet per day (MMCFD) during the 1996 fourth quarter, Beach said.
"Over time, we will focus on investing in new, higher-return opportunities, primarily overseas, but also in the U.S. Gulf Coast," he said.
Unocal's worldwide natural gas production increased seven percent in the fourth quarter, to 1,909 MMCFD.
